metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ according to the commandment of God our Savior and the Lord Jesus Christ our hope,
units.rightText: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope,
leftNotes: 1:1 NU reads Christ Jesus and omits the Lord.

units.leftText: to Timothy, my true child in faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God our Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
units.rightText: To Timothy, my true child in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord. Correcting False Teachers (Titus 1:10–16|TIT 1:10-16*)

units.leftText: As I urged you when I was going into Macedonia, stay at Ephesus that you might command certain men not to teach a different doctrine,
units.rightText: As I urged you on my departure to Macedonia, you should stay on at Ephesus to instruct certain men not to teach false doctrines

units.leftText: and not to pay attention to myths and endless genealogies, which cause disputes rather than God’s stewardship, which is in faith.
units.rightText: or devote themselves to myths and endless genealogies, which promote speculation rather than the stewardship of God’s work, which is by faith.
rightNotes: 1:4 Literally rather than the stewardship of God in faith

units.leftText: But the goal of this command is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith,
units.rightText: The goal of our instruction is the love that comes from a pure heart, a clear conscience, and a sincere faith.

units.leftText: from which things some, having missed the mark, have turned away to vain talking,
units.rightText: Some have strayed from these ways and turned aside to empty talk.

units.leftText: desiring to be teachers of the law, though they understand neither what they say nor about what they strongly affirm.
units.rightText: They want to be teachers of the law, but they do not understand what they are saying or that which they so confidently assert.

units.leftText: But we know that the law is good if a person uses it lawfully,
units.rightText: Now we know that the law is good, if one uses it legitimately.

units.leftText: as knowing this, that law is not made for a righteous person, but for the lawless and insubordinate, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,
units.rightText: We realize that law is not enacted for the righteous, but for the lawless and rebellious, for the ungodly and sinful, for the unholy and profane, for killers of father or mother, for murderers,

units.leftText: for the sexually immoral, for homosexuals, for slave-traders, for liars, for perjurers, and for any other thing contrary to the sound doctrine,
units.rightText: for the sexually immoral, for homosexuals, for slave traders and liars and perjurers, and for anyone else who is averse to sound teaching

units.leftText: according to the Good News of the glory of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.
units.rightText: that agrees with the glorious gospel of the blessed God, with which I have been entrusted. God’s Grace to Paul

units.leftText: I thank him who enabled me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he counted me faithful, appointing me to service,
units.rightText: I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who has strengthened me, that He considered me faithful and appointed me to service.

units.leftText: although I used to be a blasphemer, a persecutor, and insolent. However, I obtained mercy because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
units.rightText: I was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor, and a violent man; yet because I had acted in ignorance and unbelief, I was shown mercy.

units.leftText: The grace of our Lord abounded exceedingly with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: And the grace of our Lord overflowed to me, along with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: The saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief.
units.rightText: This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the worst.

units.leftText: However, for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first, Jesus Christ might display all his patience for an example of those who were going to believe in him for eternal life.
units.rightText: But for this very reason I was shown mercy, so that in me, the worst of sinners, Christ Jesus might display His perfect patience as an example to those who would believe in Him for eternal life.

units.leftText: Now to the King eternal, immortal, invisible, to God who alone is wise, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
units.rightText: Now to the King eternal, immortal, and invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.

units.leftText: I commit this instruction to you, my child Timothy, according to the prophecies which were given to you before, that by them you may wage the good warfare,
units.rightText: Timothy, my child, I entrust you with this command in keeping with the previous prophecies about you, so that by them you may fight the good fight,

units.leftText: holding faith and a good conscience, which some having thrust away made a shipwreck concerning the faith,
units.rightText: holding on to faith and a good conscience, which some have rejected and thereby shipwrecked their faith.

units.leftText: of whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I delivered to Satan that they might be taught not to blaspheme.
units.rightText: Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to Satan to be taught not to blaspheme.

units.leftText: I exhort therefore, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks be made for all men,
units.rightText: First of all, then, I urge that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving be offered for everyone—

units.leftText: for kings and all who are in high places, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and reverence.
units.rightText: for kings and all those in authority— so that we may lead tranquil and quiet lives in all godliness and dignity.

units.leftText: For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior,
units.rightText: This is good and pleasing in the sight of God our Savior,

units.leftText: who desires all people to be saved and come to full knowledge of the truth.
units.rightText: who wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.

units.leftText: For there is one God and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus,
units.rightText: For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus,

units.leftText: who gave himself as a ransom for all, the testimony at the proper time,
units.rightText: who gave Himself as a ransom for all — the testimony that was given at just the right time.

units.leftText: to which I was appointed a preacher and an apostle—I am telling the truth in Christ, not lying—a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
units.rightText: For this reason I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a faithful and true teacher of the Gentiles. I am telling the truth; I am not lying about anything.

units.leftText: I desire therefore that the men in every place pray, lifting up holy hands without anger and doubting.
units.rightText: Therefore I want the men everywhere to pray, lifting up holy hands, without anger or dissension. Instructions to Women

units.leftText: In the same way, that women also adorn themselves in decent clothing, with modesty and propriety, not with braided hair, gold, pearls, or expensive clothing,
units.rightText: Likewise, I want the women to adorn themselves with respectable apparel, with modesty, and with self-control, not with braided hair or gold or pearls or expensive clothes,
leftNotes: 2:9 The word for “not” is the negative particle “μη” which denies an expected idea, as opposed to the usual word for “not” (ου) which denies a fact. Thus “μη” in this context is denying an expected idea (that women can be properly dressed without good works).

units.leftText: but with good works, which is appropriate for women professing godliness.
units.rightText: but with good deeds, as is proper for women who profess to worship God.

units.leftText: Let a woman learn in quietness with full submission.
units.rightText: A woman must learn in quietness and full submissiveness.

units.leftText: But I don’t permit a woman to teach, nor to exercise authority over a man, but to be in quietness.
units.rightText: I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man; she is to remain quiet.

units.leftText: For Adam was formed first, then Eve.
units.rightText: For Adam was formed first, and then Eve.

units.leftText: Adam wasn’t deceived, but the woman, being deceived, has fallen into disobedience;
units.rightText: And it was not Adam who was deceived, but the woman who was deceived and fell into transgression.

units.leftText: but she will be saved through her childbearing, if they continue in faith, love, and holiness with sobriety.
units.rightText: Women, however, will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith, love, and holiness, with self-control.
rightNotes: 2:15 Literally She, however, will be saved

units.leftText: This is a faithful saying: someone who seeks to be an overseer desires a good work.
units.rightText: This is a trustworthy saying: If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.

units.leftText: The overseer therefore must be without reproach, the husband of one wife, temperate, sensible, modest, hospitable, good at teaching;
units.rightText: An overseer, then, must be above reproach, the husband of but one wife, temperate, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach,
rightNotes: 3:2 Or faithful to his wife; also in verse 12

units.leftText: not a drinker, not violent, not greedy for money, but gentle, not quarrelsome, not covetous;
units.rightText: not dependent on wine, not violent but gentle, peaceable, and free of the love of money.

units.leftText: one who rules his own house well, having children in subjection with all reverence;
units.rightText: An overseer must manage his own household well and keep his children under control, with complete dignity.

units.leftText: (for how could someone who doesn’t know how to rule his own house take care of God’s assembly?)
units.rightText: For if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how can he care for the church of God?

units.leftText: not a new convert, lest being puffed up he fall into the same condemnation as the devil.
units.rightText: He must not be a recent convert, or he may become conceited and fall under the same condemnation as the devil.

units.leftText: Moreover he must have good testimony from those who are outside, to avoid falling into reproach and the snare of the devil.
units.rightText: Furthermore, he must have a good reputation with outsiders, so that he will not fall into disgrace and into the snare of the devil. Qualifications for Deacons (Acts 6:1–7|ACT 6:1-7*)

units.leftText: Servants, in the same way, must be reverent, not double-tongued, not addicted to much wine, not greedy for money,
units.rightText: Deacons likewise must be dignified, not double-tongued or given to much wine or greedy for money.

units.leftText: holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
units.rightText: They must hold to the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.

units.leftText: Let them also first be tested; then let them serve if they are blameless.
units.rightText: Additionally, they must first be tested. Then, if they are above reproach, let them serve as deacons.

units.leftText: Their wives in the same way must be reverent, not slanderers, temperate, and faithful in all things.
units.rightText: In the same way, the women must be dignified, not slanderers, but temperate and faithful in all things.

units.leftText: Let servants be husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.
units.rightText: A deacon must be the husband of but one wife, a good manager of his children and of his own household.

units.leftText: For those who have served well gain for themselves a good standing and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: For those who have served well as deacons acquire for themselves a high standing and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus. The Mystery of Godliness

units.leftText: These things I write to you, hoping to come to you shortly,
units.rightText: Although I hope to come to you soon, I am writing you these things

units.leftText: but if I wait long, that you may know how men ought to behave themselves in God’s house, which is the assembly of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.
units.rightText: in case I am delayed, so that you will know how each one must conduct himself in God’s household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.

units.leftText: Without controversy, the mystery of godliness is great: God was revealed in the flesh, justified in the spirit, seen by angels, preached among the nations, believed on in the world, and received up in glory.
units.rightText: By common confession, the mystery of godliness is great: He appeared in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, was seen by angels, was proclaimed among the nations, was believed in throughout the world, was taken up in glory.
rightNotes: 3:16 Literally He who appeared; BYZ and TR God appeared

units.leftText: But the Spirit says expressly that in later times some will fall away from the faith, paying attention to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons,
units.rightText: Now the Spirit expressly states that in later times some will abandon the faith to follow deceitful spirits and the teachings of demons,

units.leftText: through the hypocrisy of men who speak lies, branded in their own conscience as with a hot iron,
units.rightText: influenced by the hypocrisy of liars, whose consciences are seared with a hot iron.

units.leftText: forbidding marriage and commanding to abstain from foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
units.rightText: They will prohibit marriage and require abstinence from certain foods that God has created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.

units.leftText: For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving.
units.rightText: For every creation of God is good, and nothing that is received with thanksgiving should be rejected,

units.leftText: For it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer.
units.rightText: because it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer. A Good Servant of Jesus Christ

units.leftText: If you instruct the brothers of these things, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished in the words of the faith and of the good doctrine which you have followed.
units.rightText: By pointing out these things to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of faith and sound instruction that you have followed.

units.leftText: But refuse profane and old wives’ fables. Exercise yourself toward godliness.
units.rightText: But reject irreverent, silly myths. Instead, train yourself for godliness.

units.leftText: For bodily exercise has some value, but godliness has value in all things, having the promise of the life which is now and of that which is to come.
units.rightText: For physical exercise is of limited value, but godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for the present life and for the one to come.

units.leftText: This saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance.
units.rightText: This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance.

units.leftText: For to this end we both labor and suffer reproach, because we have set our trust in the living God, who is the Savior of all men, especially of those who believe.
units.rightText: To this end we labor and strive, because we have set our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of everyone, and especially of those who believe.
rightNotes: 4:10 SBL, BYZ, and TR and suffer reproach

units.leftText: Command and teach these things.
units.rightText: Command and teach these things.

units.leftText: Let no man despise your youth; but be an example to those who believe, in word, in your way of life, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.
units.rightText: Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.

units.leftText: Until I come, pay attention to reading, to exhortation, and to teaching.
units.rightText: Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching.

units.leftText: Don’t neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you by prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the elders.
units.rightText: Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders.

units.leftText: Be diligent in these things. Give yourself wholly to them, that your progress may be revealed to all.
units.rightText: Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.

units.leftText: Pay attention to yourself and to your teaching. Continue in these things, for in doing this you will save both yourself and those who hear you.
units.rightText: Pay close attention to your life and to your teaching. Persevere in these things, for by so doing you will save both yourself and those who hear you.

units.leftText: Don’t rebuke an older man, but exhort him as a father; the younger men as brothers;
units.rightText: Do not rebuke an older man, but appeal to him as to a father.

units.leftText: the elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, in all purity.
units.rightText: older women as mothers, and younger women as sisters, with absolute purity. Honoring True Widows (Ruth 1:1–5|RUT 1:1-5*)

units.leftText: Honor widows who are widows indeed.
units.rightText: Honor the widows who are truly widows.

units.leftText: But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them learn first to show piety toward their own family and to repay their parents, for this is acceptable in the sight of God.
units.rightText: But if a widow has children or grandchildren, they must first learn to show godliness to their own family and repay their parents, for this is pleasing in the sight of God.

units.leftText: Now she who is a widow indeed and desolate, has her hope set on God and continues in petitions and prayers night and day.
units.rightText: The widow who is truly in need and left all alone puts her hope in God and continues night and day in her petitions and prayers.

units.leftText: But she who gives herself to pleasure is dead while she lives.
units.rightText: But she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she is still alive.

units.leftText: Also command these things, that they may be without reproach.
units.rightText: Give these instructions to the believers, so that they will be above reproach.

units.leftText: But if anyone doesn’t provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
units.rightText: If anyone does not provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

units.leftText: Let no one be enrolled as a widow under sixty years old, having been the wife of one man,
units.rightText: A widow should be enrolled if she is at least sixty years old, faithful to her husband,

units.leftText: being approved by good works, if she has brought up children, if she has been hospitable to strangers, if she has washed the saints’ feet, if she has relieved the afflicted, and if she has diligently followed every good work.
units.rightText: and well known for good deeds such as bringing up children, entertaining strangers, washing the feet of the saints, imparting relief to the afflicted, and devoting herself to every good work.

units.leftText: But refuse younger widows, for when they have grown wanton against Christ, they desire to marry,
units.rightText: But refuse to enroll younger widows. For when their passions draw them away from Christ, they will want to marry,

units.leftText: having condemnation, because they have rejected their first pledge.
units.rightText: and thus will incur judgment because they are setting aside their first faith.

units.leftText: Besides, they also learn to be idle, going about from house to house. Not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, saying things which they ought not.
units.rightText: At the same time they will also learn to be idle, going from house to house and being not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, discussing things they should not mention.

units.leftText: I desire therefore that the younger widows marry, bear children, rule the household, and give no occasion to the adversary for insulting.
units.rightText: So I advise the younger widows to marry, have children, and manage their households, denying the adversary occasion for slander.

units.leftText: For already some have turned away after Satan.
units.rightText: For some have already turned aside to follow Satan.

units.leftText: If any man or woman who believes has widows, let them relieve them, and don’t let the assembly be burdened, that it might relieve those who are widows indeed.
units.rightText: If any believing woman has dependent widows, she must assist them and not allow the church to be burdened, so that it can help the widows who are truly in need. Honoring Elders

units.leftText: Let the elders who rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in the word and in teaching.
units.rightText: Elders who lead effectively are worthy of double honor, especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.

units.leftText: For the Scripture says, “You shall not muzzle the ox when it treads out the grain.” And, “The laborer is worthy of his wages.”
units.rightText: For the Scripture says, “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain,” and, “The worker is worthy of his wages.”
rightNotes: 5:18 Luke 10:7|LUK 10:7*; see also Leviticus 19:13 and Deuteronomy 24:14–15.

units.leftText: Don’t receive an accusation against an elder except at the word of two or three witnesses.
units.rightText: Do not entertain an accusation against an elder, except on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

units.leftText: Those who sin, reprove in the sight of all, that the rest also may be in fear.
units.rightText: But those who persist in sin should be rebuked in front of everyone, so that the others will stand in fear of sin. A Charge to Timothy

units.leftText: I command you in the sight of God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the chosen angels, that you observe these things without prejudice, doing nothing by partiality.
units.rightText: I solemnly charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels to maintain these principles without bias, and to do nothing out of partiality.

units.leftText: Lay hands hastily on no one. Don’t be a participant in other people’s sins. Keep yourself pure.
units.rightText: Do not be too quick in the laying on of hands and thereby share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.

units.leftText: Be no longer a drinker of water only, but use a little wine for your stomach’s sake and your frequent infirmities.
units.rightText: Stop drinking only water and use a little wine instead, because of your stomach and your frequent ailments.

units.leftText: Some men’s sins are evident, preceding them to judgment, and some also follow later.
units.rightText: The sins of some men are obvious, going ahead of them to judgment; but the sins of others do not surface until later.

units.leftText: In the same way also there are good works that are obvious, and those that are otherwise can’t be hidden.
units.rightText: In the same way, good deeds are obvious, and even the ones that are inconspicuous cannot remain hidden.

units.leftText: Let as many as are bondservants under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honor, that the name of God and the doctrine not be blasphemed.
units.rightText: All who are under the yoke of slavery should regard their masters as fully worthy of honor, so that God’s name and our teaching will not be discredited.

units.leftText: Those who have believing masters, let them not despise them because they are brothers, but rather let them serve them, because those who partake of the benefit are believing and beloved. Teach and exhort these things.
units.rightText: Those who have believing masters should not show disrespect because they are brothers, but should serve them all the more, since those receiving their good service are beloved believers. Teach and encourage these principles. Reject False Doctrines

units.leftText: If anyone teaches a different doctrine and doesn’t consent to sound words, the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness,
units.rightText: If anyone teaches another doctrine and disagrees with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and with godly teaching,

units.leftText: he is conceited, knowing nothing, but obsessed with arguments, disputes, and word battles, from which come envy, strife, insulting, evil suspicions,
units.rightText: he is conceited and understands nothing. Instead, he has an unhealthy interest in controversies and disputes about words, out of which come envy, strife, abusive talk, evil suspicions,

units.leftText: constant friction of people of corrupt minds and destitute of the truth, who suppose that godliness is a means of gain. Withdraw yourself from such.
units.rightText: and constant friction between men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth. These men regard godliness as a means of gain. Godliness with Contentment
rightNotes: 6:5 BYZ and TR include Withdraw yourself from such.

units.leftText: But godliness with contentment is great gain.
units.rightText: Of course, godliness with contentment is great gain.

units.leftText: For we brought nothing into the world, and we certainly can’t carry anything out.
units.rightText: For we brought nothing into the world, so we cannot carry anything out of it.

units.leftText: But having food and clothing, we will be content with that.
units.rightText: But if we have food and clothing, we will be content with these.

units.leftText: But those who are determined to be rich fall into a temptation, a snare, and many foolish and harmful lusts, such as drown men in ruin and destruction.
units.rightText: Those who want to be rich, however, fall into temptation and become ensnared by many foolish and harmful desires that plunge them into ruin and destruction.

units.leftText: For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some have been led astray from the faith in their greed, and have pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
units.rightText: For the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil. By craving it, some have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows. Fight the Good Fight

units.leftText: But you, man of God, flee these things, and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.
units.rightText: But you, O man of God, flee from these things and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.

units.leftText: Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called, and you confessed the good confession in the sight of many witnesses.
units.rightText: Fight the good fight of the faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called when you made the good confession before many witnesses.

units.leftText: I command you before God who gives life to all things, and before Christ Jesus who before Pontius Pilate testified the good confession,
units.rightText: I charge you in the presence of God, who gives life to all things, and of Christ Jesus, who made the good confession in His testimony before Pontius Pilate:

units.leftText: that you keep the commandment without spot, blameless until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
units.rightText: Keep this commandment without stain or reproach until the appearance of our Lord Jesus Christ,

units.leftText: which at the right time he will show, who is the blessed and only Ruler, the King of kings and Lord of lords.
units.rightText: which the blessed and only Sovereign One— the King of kings and Lord of lords— will bring about in His own time.

units.leftText: He alone has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no man has seen nor can see, to whom be honor and eternal power. Amen.
units.rightText: He alone is immortal and dwells in unapproachable light. No one has ever seen Him, nor can anyone see Him. To Him be honor and eternal dominion! Amen. A Charge to the Rich (Proverbs 23:1–5|PRO 23:1-5*; James 5:1–6|JAS 5:1-6*)

units.leftText: Charge those who are rich in this present age that they not be arrogant, nor have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches, but on the living God, who richly provides us with everything to enjoy;
units.rightText: Instruct those who are rich in the present age not to be conceited and not to put their hope in the uncertainty of wealth, but in God, who richly provides all things for us to enjoy.

units.leftText: that they do good, that they be rich in good works, that they be ready to distribute, willing to share;
units.rightText: Instruct them to do good, to be rich in good works, and to be generous and ready to share,

units.leftText: laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold of eternal life.
units.rightText: treasuring up for themselves a firm foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of that which is truly life. Guard the Faith

units.leftText: Timothy, guard that which is committed to you, turning away from the empty chatter and oppositions of what is falsely called knowledge,
units.rightText: O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you. Avoid irreverent, empty chatter and the opposing arguments of so-called “knowledge,”

units.leftText: which some profess, and thus have wandered from the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.
units.rightText: which some have professed and thus swerved away from the faith. Grace be with you all.
